title: Insights into the planetary dynamics of HD 206893 with ALMA
question: What is the radial structure of the HD 206893 debris disc (is there a gap, asymmetry, CO gas, dust around the brown dwarf B), and what does it imply for the dynamics of the companions?

data.arrays: Band 7: ACA and 12m array; Band 6: 12m array

data.sensitivity: Image rms: Band 7 12m 9.1 uJy; Band 7 ACA 110 uJy; Band 6 12m 4.9 uJy

recipe.goal: Image the continuum and measure total flux
recipe.method: tclean Briggs imaging with Gaussian uv taper; integrate flux in an ellipse oriented as the disc
key_parameters: robust = 2.0
Gaussian taper 0.9'' at 0.88 mm and 0.4'' at 1.3 mm
assumptions: Central point source is photospheric emission (30 uJy at 0.88 mm, 13 uJy at 1.3 mm)

recipe.goal: Azimuthal radial profiles and asymmetry tests
recipe.method: Deproject with best-fit PA and inclination, azimuthally average; compare disc halves and subtract their radial profiles
key_parameters: Band 6 untapered image and band 7 image with 0.4'' taper (similar beams)
assumptions: Disc orientation from the parametric fit

recipe.goal: Reconstruct radial profile in visibility space
recipe.method: Subtract constant stellar flux from visibilities, deproject, reconstruct intensity profile with Frankenstein (Gaussian process)
key_parameters: maximum radius 400 au, alpha = 1.01, w_smooth = 1e-2
assumptions: No primary beam correction (effect < 10% within 150 au)

recipe.goal: Upper limit on dust around the brown dwarf B
recipe.method: Search for a point source at the expected BD position; 3 sigma flux limits converted to dust mass with radiative transfer
key_parameters: BD expected at ~0.25'' separation towards the NE
Dust accretion rate onto BD from the debris disc ~4 kg/s using Bonsor et al. 2018 with corrected K_ej = 5.14e8
assumptions: Disc size >~0.1 au (a smaller, optically thick disc could hide more mass)
Accreted dust: 1 um radius grains, 3 g/cm3, accreted for 700 Myr

recipe.goal: Search for CO emission and derive CO mass and ice fraction limits
recipe.method: Continuum-subtract, image cubes with tclean, apply a Keplerian mask (both rotation senses), integrate within deprojected radius of 150 au, convert flux limits to CO mass with a non-LTE tool, then to CO+CO2 ice fraction
software: CO mass tool of Matra et al. 2018
key_parameters: Band 7 cubes 0.43 km/s channels (1.1 km/s effective); Band 6 cubes 1.3 km/s channels (2.0 km/s effective)
Kinetic temperatures 20 to 200 K
assumptions: Optically thin CO emission, non-LTE excitation
Fractional luminosity ~3e-4, stellar mass 1.3 Msun, luminosity 2.9 Lsun, disc radius 70 au and width 100 au, photodissociation timescale 120 yr

recipe.goal: Fit parametric gap disc model to visibilities
recipe.method: Two-power-law surface density with Gaussian gap, radiative transfer with RADMC-3D, MCMC fit in visibility space
key_parameters: Gap depth fixed to 1
Vertical extent fixed to 5% of radius, uniform vertical mass distribution
r_min lower limit of 14 au; outer edge fixed at 250 au
Free parameters include disc inclination and PA, phase centre offsets, and position, size (2D Gaussian) and flux of a background SMG ~11.5'' to the SW; spectral index alpha free and uniform
Reported values are posterior medians with 16th and 84th percentile uncertainties
assumptions: Dust mass counts only grains smaller than 1 cm, set by assumed opacities
Star modelled with Teff = 6500 K and R = 1.3 Rsun template spectrum

recipe.goal: Convert gap width to planet mass
recipe.method: Gap width equated to chaotic zone width w_g = 3 a_p mu^(2/7), using posterior of r_g and w_g
key_parameters: Stellar mass 1.3 Msun
assumptions: Gap truly empty and cleared by a planet on a circular orbit through scattering

recipe.goal: Fit the orbit of B with the disc orientation as prior
recipe.method: Orbitize parallel-tempering MCMC on published astrometry with normal priors on inclination and node from the disc fit
key_parameters: Priors: inclination N(140 deg, 3 deg), longitude of ascending node N(61 deg, 4 deg); SE side of the disc is the near side
10^7 points after convergence
assumptions: B's orbit is co-planar with the disc

recipe.goal: Constrain mass and semi-major axis of inner companion C
recipe.method: Combine proper motion anomaly, RV acceleration, direct imaging limits and a stability criterion; Monte Carlo bootstrapping of the PMa and disc orientation; N-body check with REBOUND
key_parameters: Stability limit: orbital spacing smaller than 5 mutual Hill radii, B circular with 12 MJup
Minimum RV acceleration 45 m/s/yr
assumptions: Disc inclination (40 deg) used as the system inclination

recipe.goal: Test gap origin and disc stirring scenarios
recipe.method: Analytic secular resonance locations (Yelverton et al. 2018), disc mass from a collisional model, stirring timescales (Mustill & Wyatt 2009; Krivov et al. 2018)
key_parameters: Equation 13 of Yelverton et al. 2018 has a typo; corrected first factor a_1^(1/2) a_2^2 a^(-5/2)
Maximum planetesimal size 100 km (or 400 km), disc age 50-700 Myr
assumptions: Yelverton et al. analysis valid only for two planets and a massless disc
